newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil slips into contango.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil slips into contango.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps slipped into contango late afternoon on Monday amid strong prompt selling pressure as the market grappled with the surplus supplies in the wake of thin demand, traders said.
"The market is under pressure as there are a lot of surplus prompt supplies around and demand is very weak," one trader said.
The February/March time spread traded at minus 75 cents, one broker said.
Traders said this was the first time the fuel oil swaps market is in contango in months.
February swaps were last quoted at $106.75/107.75 a tonne, down from this morning's $107.50/$109.50, brokers said. March was quoted at $107.25/$108.25, they said.
The market weakness was blamed on high stock levels in Hong Kong and China where some storage terminals were reporting "tank top" situation, traders said.
Others report a price war breaking out in the Singapore bunker market with sellers undercutting each other in an effort to secure greater market share.
Gas oil swaps firmed slightly but the market is still in contango, reflecting the bearish prompt market fundamentals.
"The market is bogged down by the over supply of prompt cargoes and China is still not buying any large cargoes," one trader said.
February gas oil swaps were last quoted at $27.30/$27.40 per barrel, slightly firmer than morning levels of $27.15/$27.25, one broker said.
The market traded this morning at $27.20 and $27.15 a barrel, he said.
March was quoted at $27.50/$27.60 from $27.30/$27.50 in the morning. Brokers said the February/March time spread was quoted at minus 15-35 cents.

Traders said the current cut in refinery runs by two Singapore refiners was not likely to have an immediate impact as it would take the market at least another one to two weeks to digest all the prompt oversupply.
Shell Singapore said it had cut runs by 30,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) or about seven per cent of its 420,000-bpd capacity. Exxon reduced runs in Singapore by 20-25 percent of its 230,000-bpd capacity.
Naphtha was notionally quoted weaker due to the big crude fall with February seen at $23.10/$23.40 from $23.80/$24.10 on Friday, one broker said.
